summary: The 71 new identifiers are correct -- every one independently re-derived from the cached POM (following parents) and every one matches. `./gradlew dependencyLicenses` MEASURED green in the reviewer tree (BUILD SUCCESSFUL, stamp `ok 122 jar(s)`). Scope was not narrowed: build.gradle.kts, buildSrc/ and gradle/libs.versions.toml are untouched, and licenses/SPDX.txt is add-only. The `53 of 71`, `18 fallbacks` and the 8-name placeholder list are MEASURED exact. One major: the manifest is now certified green over junit:junit:4.13.2, which the pre-existing `junit EPL-2.0` line mis-identifies -- its POM declares Eclipse Public License 1.0.

findings.title: `junit EPL-2.0` is the wrong identifier for junit:junit:4.13.2, which this commit's green gate now certifies
findings.failure_scenario: junit:junit:4.13.2 resolves into licenseCheck (transitively via org.opensearch.test:framework; confirmed at line 284 of `gradlew dependencies --configuration licenseCheck`). Its jar is junit-4.13.2.jar, so DependencyLicensesTask.prefixFor yields base `junit` -- which `^junit-.*` does NOT full-match -- and it lands on the pre-existing prefix `junit`. That prefix declares EPL-2.0 and its licences/junit-LICENSE.txt is the EPL-2.0 text. junit 4.13.2's published POM declares `<name>Eclipse Public License 1.0</name>`, url http://www.eclipse.org/legal/epl-v10.html (MEASURED from the cached POM). EPL-1.0 and EPL-2.0 are different licences: EPL-2.0 adds the Secondary Licenses clause and changes the patent-defence trigger. Two concrete consequences. (1) The attribution half of build.md rule 2 ships the wrong licence's text for junit 4. (2) The identifier is what `denied` is matched against; the deny list already carries CDDL-1.0, an equally weak-copyleft licence, so adding EPL-1.0 is a plausible future edit -- and when it happens junit 4.13.2 passes green under an EPL-2.0 label while the gate reports it as reviewed. This is the exact failure mode the staged notes name ("a wrong identifier is worse than a missing one"), and the same notes assert "EVERY IDENTIFIER COMES FROM THE ARTIFACT'S PUBLISHED POM" -- which is false for this jar, so the claim is also a non-negotiable-4 overstatement about a file the diff modifies. Not introduced by the diff, but this is the commit that makes `dependencyLicenses` green for the first time in 10 CI runs; after it, nothing re-derives. Fix is small and WIDENS the gate: add `"^junit$" to "junit4"` to licenceMappings, commit licenses/junit4-LICENSE.txt (EPL-1.0 text), add `junit4 EPL-1.0`. Or argue it in a staged baselines/review.txt with a backlog row.

findings.title: The new `framework` and `telemetry` prefixes are group-blind and generically named
findings.failure_scenario: DependencyLicensesTask.prefixFor derives the prefix from the JAR FILENAME only; the Maven group is never consulted. This diff adds `framework Apache-2.0` (line 34) and `telemetry Apache-2.0` (line 99) for org.opensearch.test:framework and org.opensearch.test:telemetry -- both artifactIds generic enough to collide. A future dependency from any other group shipping `framework-<version>.jar` maps to prefix `framework`, finds the committed Apache-2.0 line and framework-LICENSE.txt, and passes `dependencyLicenses` green with its own licence never declared by anyone. If that dependency were GPL-2.0-only, the deny list would never see it: it matches the identifier looked up by prefix, not the artifact. The existing `junit`/`helidon` prefixes have the same property, so this is a widening of a pre-existing surface rather than a new one, and the real fix (keying on group:artifact, not filename) belongs with M0.19, which build.gradle.kts already names as the row that makes classpath completeness a predicate.

verified: MEASURED: ./gradlew dependencyLicenses in the reviewer tree -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, build/dependency-licenses.stamp = 'ok 122 jar(s)'.

MEASURED: scope not narrowed. git diff --cached --name-only contains no build.gradle.kts, no buildSrc/, no gradle/libs.versions.toml, no settings.gradle.kts. licenses/SPDX.txt is add-only (no line removed). The only deletion is licenses/byte-buddy-1.15.11.jar.sha1, which is genuinely stale: byte-buddy resolves at 1.18.8 and licenses/byte-buddy-1.18.8.jar.sha1 already existed; 122 pins now match 122 resolved jars exactly.

MEASURED: all 71 new identifiers re-derived independently from the POMs in the Gradle cache, following <parent> where the child declares no <licenses>. Every one agrees. Spot-checks on the four dual-licensed: jakarta.annotation-api-1.3.5 POM = 'EPL 2.0 | GPL2 w/ CPE' (EPL-2.0 taken, legitimate); jna-5.16.0 POM = 'LGPL-2.1-or-later | Apache-2.0' and the jar's own LICENSE reads 'SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1' (Apache-2.0 taken, legitimate); HdrHistogram-2.2.2 POM = 'Public Domain, per CC0 | BSD-2-Clause' (BSD-2-Clause taken, legitimate); jts-core-1.15.0 POM = 'Eclipse Publish License 1.0 | Eclipse Distribution License - v 1.0' and EDL-1.0 is verbatim BSD-3-Clause (legitimate). Taking the permissive side of a genuine disjunctive grant is a choice the licensor offers, not an exception, so build.md rule 3 does NOT require a baselines/licenses.txt line for any of the four -- rule 3's exception is for a dependency that would otherwise fail the gate, and none of these would.
MEASURED: no denied identifier is reachable. None of the 76 prefixes maps to any member of the `denied` set in build.gradle.kts.

MEASURED: the attribution accounting is exact, not approximate. Comparing each committed text against META-INF licence entries in the corresponding jars: 53 of 71 are byte-equal to the jar's own text; 3 (jackson-dataformat-cbor/-smile/-yaml) ship a META-INF licence that differs; 15 ship none. 3+15 = the 18 claimed fallbacks. Of those 18, exactly 8 are MIT/BSD -- hamcrest, jopt-simple, jts-core, jzlib, mockito-core, protobuf-java, reactive-streams, zstd-jni-1.5.6 -- and all 8 do carry '<copyright holders>'/'<owner>' placeholders; the other 10 are Apache-2.0. That is precisely the list SPDX.txt names. HdrHistogram and slf4j-api are correctly NOT in it: both ship real attributed texts.

JUDGEMENT on the attribution limitation: disclosing it is sufficient, not blocking. All 8 placeholder artifacts are transitives of compileOnly OpenSearch/test-only dependencies that this project does not redistribute today, so no attribution obligation is currently breached; and the SPDX identifier -- the machine-checkable half of build.md rule 2 -- is unaffected. Recording it in SPDX.txt beats a file that looks complete. Worth a backlog row for when the plugin distribution is assembled, not a block now.
